A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dolphin framework and contain 23 readable pages, including Appendices A–H. Text extraction, rendered-page comparison and inspection of embedded graphics support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports original accuracy and training-time experiments in Section 4, plus provenance comparisons, sensitivity analyses and additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results and revises two baseline accuracy results in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The Dolphin abstractions, primitives, CPU/GPU execution procedure, DAMP and DTKP-AM provenances, and training objective are unchanged, including their appendix descriptions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MNIST SumN, HWF, PathFinder, CLUTRR and Mugen coverage, together with the MNIST ProductN experiments in Appendix G.

E2.justification: Scallop, LTN, ISED and IndeCateR+ retain the same participation in corresponding comparisons. ISED is already evaluated on HWF-7 and HWF-15 in v5; only its plotted results change.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 and the appendices retain the same splits, models, hyperparameters, metrics and testing procedures. Figure 5 retains its ten-hour training limit; no protocol revision or experimental rerun is documented.

E4.justification: The provenance ablations, CPU/GPU timing analysis, top-k sensitivity study, no-timeout evaluation and combinatorial-scaling experiments are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report three trials and average best accuracy and training time. Figure 5 retains error bars; the changed numerical extents for two results do not establish a change in statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Under Figure 5's unchanged settings, ISED's plotted HWF-7 accuracy changes from approximately 6.36% to 97.51%, and HWF-15 from 6.43% to 98.89%, with revised error-bar extents. Both now exceed Dolphin's unchanged means of approximately 96.25% and 92.13%. These large shifts substantially revise the baseline comparison and rankings; other results, including Figure 7, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, provenance operations, assumptions and derivations in Section 3 and Appendices A and C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about programmability, scalability, efficiency and state-of-the-art accuracy. These claims are not revised alongside Figure 5.

C2.justification: The interpretations of baseline performance and provenance behavior, applicability discussion and stated limitations are unchanged. Sections 4.4 and D.2 do not explain or reconcile the revised ISED results.

D1.justification: Hardware descriptions, implementation listings, hyperparameters, dataset preparation details and code-access information are unchanged. No technical explanation accompanies the revised accuracy values.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion and positioning against other neurosymbolic frameworks are unchanged, including the appendix comparisons.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v5 dated 29 Oct 2025 to v6 dated 29 Dec 2025. The document's prose, terminology and section structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figure 5 retains its axes, legend, caption, grouping, styling and placement; its changed bar heights and error-bar extents represent the result changes assessed under E6. Other figures, tables and page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v6 weakens internal consistency: Figure 5 now places ISED above Dolphin on two HWF variants, while Section 4.4 still identifies CLUTRR as the only accuracy exception. Appendix D.2 and the no-timeout Figure 7 retain low ISED results without explaining their relationship to the revised near-98% accuracies. The PDFs do not establish whether the new values correct earlier errors, but the unreconciled evidence and narrative constitute a supported reporting-quality decline.
